name: Tree service

pf.license.need: if: a tree care license, a tree expert license or a tree care registration for the company, where the state's form or the city requires one; a pesticide applicator license for any spraying or trunk injection, in every state
ask: The company's tree care license or registration number, where the state or city has one
Each sprayer's pesticide applicator license number and category
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
Any arborist certificate the business wants shown (it shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie)
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No tree work goes live until the company's license or registration checks out, where one is required
Spraying never goes live without a licensed sprayer on the team
Work near power lines is never offered: only the utility or a line-clearance crew may do it
pf.license.renewals: License, registry, insurance and applicator dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings for that work
pf.license.trust: 'Certified arborist' or 'insured' shows only once Rosie has read the certificate or the official lookup; otherwise it's the business's own words
pf.license.wood_yard: A firewood, wood chip and mulch yard needs no state license; its business registration is checked. Firewood sold by the cord or face cord, with a written receipt, where the state's rules require it.
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

pf.services.pattern: Arborist visit, then project: a tree removal is booked as the arborist's visit, then a written quote, a signed contract and a job day

B.name: Arborist visit (the estimate)
B.price: $89, credited to the job if Alex signs (the example business's own price; a free estimate is the plug-in's starting answer)
B.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home
B.after: billed only if no contract follows

B.name: Tree removal
B.price: quoted after the arborist visit, in writing, good for 30 days
B.length: one job day, 8am to 3pm; a crane job may take two
B.before: nothing at booking; a deposit once the contract is signed
B.after: the rest on the bill after the walk-through

B.name: Pruning
B.price: quoted after the arborist visit, or from the list for a small tree
B.season: no oak pruning April to July (the example business's own oak wilt practice)

B.name: Small tree removal
B.price: priced from photos for a small tree with nothing near it (example: $640); over $500, Sam OKs it
B.before: a signed estimate, then a 25% deposit

B.name: Stump grinding
B.price: $179 a stump up to 2 feet across, from the list; bigger ones quoted
B.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home

B.name: Storm work
B.price: sent now, with an arrival estimate; priced before anyone climbs
B.on_call: an arborist on call nights and weekends

B.name: Brush pile pickup
B.where: outside; nobody needs to be home

B.name: Lift or crane
B.price: a tracked lift is part of the job when it fits the gate; a crane is quoted on its own line

B.name: Wood
B.price: hauled away (included), or left in rounds at no charge

B.name: Tree spraying (Lee Plant Health)
B.price: ash tree injection $149, deep root feeding $189; orchard spraying quoted

B.name: Work near power lines
B.price: not offered: the utility or a line-clearance crew

Brush drop-off (a pickup load)

Log milling (your log sawn into boards)

pf.services.capacity: One arborist per arborist visit; one big job per crew a day, with the lift, the chipper and the grinder booked with it; one loader and one sawmill at the yard
pf.services.skills: Arborist visits and quotes: the arborist (Eli). Climbing and removals: a crew with a crew lead. Stumps: anyone trained on the grinder. Spraying: licensed sprayers only. The yard: Nell and Wes; the sawmill and the log splitter: Nell only.
pf.services.nobody_home: Arborist visits, stump grinding and brush pickups: nobody needs to be home (DONE with a photo). A removal: an adult walks the job with the crew at the start, where possible.
pf.services.months: Each service can carry the months it's offered (the example: no oak pruning April to July)

before_times: What should be done? (take down, prune, grind a stump, storm damage)
Is any part of the tree within 10 feet of a power line? (no; only the line to the house; street lines)
About how tall is the tree, and how wide is the trunk?
Is it leaning, cracked or dead?
after_time: Whose tree is it? (yours; on the property line; someone else's)
Is it on the city strip by the street?
How wide is the gate to the yard? Any pets?
The wood and the stump: hauled away or left; ground or left
Will you be home for the arborist visit? (not needed)
secure_page_only: Private buried lines near the stump (sprinklers, a dog fence, yard lights)
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the tree. A tree on the property line needs the neighbor's yes too, given on the secure page. Someone else's tree, or a renter's, is booked or OK'd by its owner.
yard: What are you bringing: a pickup or a trailer, and how long is the bed?
For milling or splitting: how many logs, and photos of them

stop.words: a limb or tree on a power line, wires down, sparks, a tree touching the street lines
stop.says: Stay far away, and keep everyone back. Call 911 and the electric company. Only the utility or a line-clearance crew may work on it.

stop.words: someone hurt or trapped, a gas smell after a tree fell
stop.says: Call 911 now, and leave the area if you smell gas.

steps_then_go_on.words: a tree or a big limb on the house or the garage
steps_then_go_on.says: Get everyone out of the rooms under it, and keep them out. Don't go on the roof or cut anything. Call 911 first if anyone is hurt, wires are down or you smell gas.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on, marked urgent; sent now where the business takes storm work

steps_then_go_on.words: a tree leaning more, or a new crack at the base
steps_then_go_on.says: Keep people and cars away from the side it leans toward.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; the soonest time is offered

steps_then_go_on.words: a gas line marked near a stump
steps_then_go_on.says: Nobody grinds inside the marked zone.
steps_then_go_on.booking: the grinding stops there; a partial grind or none, with Alex's yes

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether a tree is safe to climb or cut yourself go to the business's own line

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The arborist visit at the property (nobody needs to be home)
pf.first_steps.power_lines: Only the line to the house within 10 feet: the customer asks the utility to make it safe for the job day; the arborist visit goes ahead, but no job day is set until the utility's date is known
after_contract: The cancel window ends before the job day, where the state's rules give one
A city tree permit, where the city protects the tree or it's on the city strip: Sam applies, and the job day waits for it
The 811 locate before any stump is ground: Sam places it, keeps its ticket number on the job, and the marks come before the job day (the lead time is the state's)
The utility's date, when only the line to the house was near the tree
prep: Mark any private buried lines near the stump (sprinklers, a dog fence, yard lights): 811 marks only the utilities' lines
Move cars away from the tree and the drop zone the night before
Unlock the gate, and keep pets inside
yard_prep: Bring a truck or trailer that can carry the load, with the bed empty
Bring a tarp to cover the load, where the state's rules require loads to be covered

pf.visit.check_in: The arborist visit and each job day: the check-in code at the door or the gate, or DONE with a photo when nobody is home. The yard: the code at the yard office.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The arborist looks at the trunk, the height, the lean and the condition, checks the city's tree rules, and checks that the lift fits the gate. The written quote follows within a day, good for 30 days.
pf.visit.on_the_job_day: Walk the job with the customer; ground mats from the gate; check the 811 paint and the customer's flags; rope off the work area; branches first, then the trunk in short sections lowered away from buildings; brush straight into the chipper; before and after photos
pf.visit.changes: Extra work (another tree, a dead limb) is priced and OK'd in writing before it's done. Less work (a partial grind by a gas line) is priced down, with the customer's yes.
pf.visit.done: The walk-through against the quote, line by line; ruts from the lift leveled and seeded before leaving; then DONE
pf.visit.yard_done: The load leveled and tarped, shown to the customer before paying; DONE with the load's photo
pf.visit.before_photos: The lawn by the gate, the driveway, the fence, the garden beds and anything already damaged

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 arborist visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the plug-in's starting answer.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On a removal quoted at the visit, nothing is taken before the contract is signed
pf.money.deposit: A deposit when the quote is signed (the example: 10%), within the state's deposit cap
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.last_payment: After the walk-through, on the bill Rosie texts: pay link, card, bank transfer for big bills, or a check
pf.money.cancel: The example's policy: a full refund until 48 hours before the job day; later, Sam may keep the deposit, and he confirms each time
pf.money.weather: A job moved for wind or ice costs nothing, and cancelling stays free
pf.money.storms: Storm prices stay inside the state's limits during a declared emergency
pf.money.yard: The $20 missed-loading fee ($40 for log milling) only after Sam OKs it; paid at the yard office

never_in_texts: Contract and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who walks the job with the crew

pf.staff.roles: Eli: the arborist, who does arborist visits and quotes and leads the crew. Hugo: crew lead, stumps and storm work on call. Nell and Wes at the yard; only Nell runs the sawmill and the log splitter.
pf.staff.line_clearance: Only line-clearance-qualified crews work near power lines; this business has none, so that work is never offered
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes, change orders and job days over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.weather_call: The crew lead may move a job day for wind or ice
pf.staff.stand_in: Hugo may take an arborist visit for a stump or pruning; a removal keeps its arborist unless Sam moves it

pf.rules.contract: A written quote and contract before any tree removal, where the state's rules require one (and always in the example), signed by the tree's owner and the business before any money
pf.rules.where_signed: A yes that follows a visit at the property counts as a sale at the home wherever it is signed, so the cancel notice goes out, until each state's rule is read
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; the job day waits for it
pf.rules.tree_permits: City tree permits for protected trees or trees on the city strip, where the city requires one
pf.rules.locate: The 811 locate before any digging or stump grinding, with the state's own lead time and ticket life; a moved job day re-checks it
pf.rules.power_lines: No work within the state's distance of power lines unless the crew is line-clearance qualified
pf.rules.show: The license or registry number on the listing, the quote and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.guarantee: Cleanup or damage the crew missed is fixed free within 30 days (the example's)

pf.edges.power_line_to_house: The arborist visit goes ahead; the job day waits for the utility's date
pf.edges.street_lines: No booking: only the utility or a line-clearance crew
pf.edges.boundary_tree: The neighbor's yes on the secure page before the removal; the arborist visit can go ahead
pf.edges.someone_elses_tree: No booking; the customer forwards a link to the tree's owner
pf.edges.permit_pending: The job day waits for the city's OK; moved with no fee
pf.edges.no_locate_marks: The tree still comes down on the job day; only the grinding moves, and the customer is told
pf.edges.wind_or_ice: Over the lift's limit on the job day: the job moves to the next free day, no fee
pf.edges.storm_before_job_day: A limb falls on a building before the job day: the safety steps, the job moved up where the crew is free, and any extra signed first
pf.edges.gas_line_by_stump: A partial grind at a lower price, or none, with the customer's yes
pf.edges.lift_ruts: Leveled and seeded before the crew leaves
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

story.B: Sam Lee signs up two companies by text. Then Alex books Lee Tree Care for a dead ash leaning toward the garage at 19 Hillcrest Rd. Eli, the arborist, looks at it Thu Oct 22 between 8 and 10am, sends a written quote, and his crew takes the tree down on the job day once the contract is signed. The money choice you pick changes the path.

notes:
Pilot: started from the contractor (pattern project). A tree job runs the same way: an arborist visit at the property, a written quote, a signed contract with a deposit, then the work on a later day. What the contractor lacked, the overlay adds: the power-line check, whose tree it is, the 811 locate, the job day's own what-ifs and check-in.
Flow B (main path visit|none|bill): Alex's dead ash leaning toward the garage at 19 Hillcrest Rd. The $89 arborist visit Thu Oct 22 (nothing taken, credited to the job if Alex signs); Eli's written quote of $2,100 (B8-20 words); the contract signed by Alex and Sam (B8-62); the $210 deposit and the job day Thu Oct 29 (B8-63); then the own steps B8-x01 to B8-x14: the cancel window, Sam's 811 locate to-do (with a city permit and missing marks as what-ifs), the day-before reminder with its own code, what can change before the job day, the crew's check-in and the take-down. The last $1,890 is the bill Rosie texts (B9-05 to B9-11 words); receipt, rating and the 30-day cleanup guarantee follow (B10 words).
The example's $89 arborist visit keeps the master's $89 numbers and fee math. The old flow's free estimate is the plug-in's starting answer (pf.money estimate, pf.services). The old flow's numbers stay: $2,100 total, a 10% deposit of $210, a $1,890 rest, job day Thu Oct 29.
B8-20's '1 Yes, fix it', '3 OK some lines' and 'Over the landlord's top amount' are off (B9-27's '3 OK some lines' too): a removal never starts at the arborist visit, its quote is signed whole (the wood and stump lines are picked on the quote's page), and a renter's tree is the landlord's to sign. Rename pairs give the master branches '1 Signs the contract' and 'No reply in 5 days', so the quote's buttons (Sign the contract, Not now) match the branch numbers.
Dates: the cancel window ends 11:59pm Tue Oct 27, before the job day; Sam's 48-hour cancel policy (pf.money cancel) also ends by then, so a cancel the day before goes to Sam for the deposit (B8-x12). The storm what-if moves the job up to Wed Oct 28, after the window. Extra work found on the job day gets its own dates (B8-24, B8-25, B10-05, B10-06 words: cancel until Mon Nov 2, quote good until Thu Nov 5).
Where the yes was given: Alex signed on his phone away from home, but the quote followed Eli's visit there, so B8-x01 treats it as a sale at the home (Rosie's safe default, a rule box). No state's number of days is written; the window's date is the example's.
Power lines: B4-x01 asks on every tree job before any time (pf.questions). Only the line to the house: the visit goes ahead, the job day waits for the utility (B4-x02). Street lines: no booking (B4-x03). The 10-foot distance is the plug-in's question; no law is cited.
Whose tree: B4-35 words plus two branches (B4-x04 the neighbor's yes for a tree on the property line; B4-x05 someone else's tree, not booked). B4-78's '2 No: nobody asks' is off: tree work always asks.
811 locate: the business's own first step. On the main path it's Sam's to-do after signing (B8-x03, the ticket number kept on the job); on the stump path (list|hold|bill) it's the master's 'The business gets it first' (B4-42 words) with the lead time (B4-87 words). Missing marks move only the grinding (B8-x05). No state's lead time is written.
Money combinations used: B visit|none|bill, visit|none|own, list|hold|bill (a stump grinding from the list, $179, with the $89 visit fee held, the plug-in's starting answer for work at the customer's place paid after, as in Sam's sign-up setup), photos|deposit|bill (a small crabapple priced from photos at $640, a signed estimate, a $160 deposit). A list|card|counter, list|none|counter, list|full|none, list|deposit|counter. Left out: the saved card charged at DONE (tree bills are paid by link, transfer or check), the visit hold (the old flow takes nothing before the quote), A's photo and at-the-yard pricing (kept only as examples).
Words ops on the visit path set the full combination keys (price:visit+before:none+after:bill and +after:own); the build also writes the same words onto every master vary key that only those two combinations light, so no plumber words show on the page.
Flow A is Sam's second company, Lee Wood Yard (the master's Lee's Barbershop): firewood, wood chips and mulch picked up at the yard, 4 Quarry Ln. Main path list|card|counter: a $35 pickup load of wood chips with Nell, Sat Oct 24 11:00am, a card saved for the $20 missed-loading fee, paid at the yard office. The yard's board keeps the barbershop's prices: wood chips $35, mulch $40, brush drop-off $20, kindling crate $25, half a face cord of firewood $55 (paid in full), log milling $140 for 2½ hours ($40 deposit), log splitting from photos $90, slab cutting at the yard after a $25 log check. Delivery to a home ($75) is the other flow.
Flow A ops: A8-02 keeps both branches (splitsKept): the yard checks for a truck bed that fits the load and a tarp, and a trailer too small for the load is 'Something required is missing' (rename pairs). A4-43 keeps only 'No' and A7-02's first-step branches are off: a pickup has no first step. A7-70 keeps 'Shorter, in the time left' (a late truck is loaded in the time left, or moves).
